You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE conductor (
    Conductor_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Age INT,
    Nationality TEXT,
    Year_of_Work INT,
    UNIQUE (Conductor_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE orchestra (
    Orchestra_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Orchestra TEXT,
    Conductor_ID INT,
    Record_Company TEXT,
    Year_of_Founded REAL,
    Major_Record_Format TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Orchestra_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Conductor_ID) REFERENCES conductor(Conductor_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE performance (
    Performance_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Orchestra_ID INT,
    Type TEXT,
    Date TEXT,
    Official_ratings_(millions) REAL,
    Weekly_rank TEXT,
    Share TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Performance_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Orchestra_ID) REFERENCES orchestra(Orchestra_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE show (
    Show_ID INT,
    Performance_ID INT,
    If_first_show bool,
    Result TEXT,
    Attendance REAL,
    FOREIGN KEY (Performance_ID) REFERENCES performance(Performance_ID)
);

There isn’t a “famous” flag/column in your schema, so we have to define “famous” using something measurable in the data. Here are a few common options (pick one), with SQL:

### 1) Conductors with the highest total official ratings (sum over their performances)
```sql
SELECT
  c.Conductor_ID,
  c.Name,
  SUM(p."Official_ratings_(millions)") AS total_ratings_millions
FROM conductor c
JOIN orchestra o  ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
JOIN performance p ON p.Orchestra_ID = o.Orchestra_ID
GROUP BY c.Conductor_ID, c.Name
ORDER BY total_ratings_millions DESC;
```

### 2) Conductors with the most performances
```sql
SELECT
  c.Conductor_ID,
  c.Name,
  COUNT(*) AS performance_count
FROM conductor c
JOIN orchestra o  ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
JOIN performance p ON p.Orchestra_ID = o.Orchestra_ID
GROUP BY c.Conductor_ID, c.Name
ORDER BY performance_count DESC;
```

### 3) Conductors with the biggest single performance rating
```sql
SELECT
  c.Conductor_ID,
  c.Name,
  MAX(p."Official_ratings_(millions)") AS peak_rating_millions
FROM conductor c
JOIN orchestra o  ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
JOIN performance p ON p.Orchestra_ID = o.Orchestra_ID
GROUP BY c.Conductor_ID, c.Name
ORDER BY peak_rating_millions DESC;
```

Which definition do you want (highest total ratings, most performances, or highest single rating), and do you want a top N (e.g., top 10)?
Just give me the names of the famous conductors based on their ratings or performances or whatever.

Since “famous” isn’t explicitly stored, here are conductor names that rank highly by **either total ratings** or **number of performances** (union of the top 10 in each):

```sql
WITH by_ratings AS (
  SELECT c.Name
  FROM conductor c
  JOIN orchestra o  ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
  JOIN performance p ON p.Orchestra_ID = o.Orchestra_ID
  GROUP BY c.Conductor_ID, c.Name
  ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(p."Official_ratings_(millions)"), 0) DESC
  LIMIT 10
),
by_performances AS (
  SELECT c.Name
  FROM conductor c
  JOIN orchestra o  ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
  JOIN performance p ON p.Orchestra_ID = o.Orchestra_ID
  GROUP BY c.Conductor_ID, c.Name
  ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
  LIMIT 10
)
SELECT DISTINCT Name
FROM (
  SELECT Name FROM by_ratings
  UNION ALL
  SELECT Name FROM by_performances
) x
ORDER BY Name;
```
Make sure the conductors have worked with multiple orchestras, not just one.

```sql
WITH multi_orchestra_conductors AS (
  SELECT c.Conductor_ID, c.Name
  FROM conductor c
  JOIN orchestra o ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
  GROUP BY c.Conductor_ID, c.Name
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.Orchestra_ID) >= 2
),
by_ratings AS (
  SELECT m.Name
  FROM multi_orchestra_conductors m
  JOIN orchestra o  ON o.Conductor_ID = m.Conductor_ID
  JOIN performance p ON p.Orchestra_ID = o.Orchestra_ID
  GROUP BY m.Conductor_ID, m.Name
  ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(p."Official_ratings_(millions)"), 0) DESC
  LIMIT 10
),
by_performances AS (
  SELECT m.Name
  FROM multi_orchestra_conductors m
  JOIN orchestra o  ON o.Conductor_ID = m.Conductor_ID
  JOIN performance p ON p.Orchestra_ID = o.Orchestra_ID
  GROUP BY m.Conductor_ID, m.Name
  ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
  LIMIT 10
)
SELECT DISTINCT Name
FROM (
  SELECT Name FROM by_ratings
  UNION ALL
  SELECT Name FROM by_performances
) x
ORDER BY Name;
```
only consider conductors based on their past conducting activities

If “past conducting activities” means conductors who **actually have performance records** (not just listed in `orchestra`), filter to conductors with performances and (as requested) multiple orchestras:

```sql
WITH active_multi_orchestra AS (
  SELECT
    c.Conductor_ID,
    c.Name
  FROM conductor c
  JOIN orchestra o  ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
  JOIN performance p ON p.Orchestra_ID = o.Orchestra_ID
  GROUP BY c.Conductor_ID, c.Name
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.Orchestra_ID) >= 2
),
by_ratings AS (
  SELECT a.Name
  FROM active_multi_orchestra a
  JOIN orchestra o  ON o.Conductor_ID = a.Conductor_ID
  JOIN performance p ON p.Orchestra_ID = o.Orchestra_ID
  GROUP BY a.Conductor_ID, a.Name
  ORDER BY SUM(COALESCE(p."Official_ratings_(millions)"), 0)) DESC
  LIMIT 10
),
by_performances AS (
  SELECT a.Name
  FROM active_multi_orchestra a
  JOIN orchestra o  ON o.Conductor_ID = a.Conductor_ID
  JOIN performance p ON p.Orchestra_ID = o.Orchestra_ID
  GROUP BY a.Conductor_ID, a.Name
  ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
  LIMIT 10
)
SELECT DISTINCT Name
FROM (
  SELECT Name FROM by_ratings
  UNION ALL
  SELECT Name FROM by_performances
) x
ORDER BY Name;
```

If you instead mean “past” as in **before today** (based on `performance.Date`), tell me the date format stored in `performance.Date` (e.g., `YYYY-MM-DD`).
